{{recipesummary|category=Confection recipes|yield=36|time=1 hour|difficulty=2}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Mexico|Mexican cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Native American cuisine|Native American cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|Vegetarian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]]

==Ingredients==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Coffee|instant coffee powder]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiling]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 10 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] best-quality semisweet [[Cookbook:Chocolate|chocolate]], in small pieces or chips
* 10 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] (1¼ sticks) best-quality unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], cold and cut into small pieces
* 2–3 [[Cookbook:Jalapeño|jalapeños]], roasted, peeled, seeded, and finely [[Cookbook:Chop|chopped]] (wear rubber gloves)
* ½ cup unsweetened [[Cookbook:Cocoa Powder|cocoa powder]], [[Cookbook:Sift|sift]] onto a plate

==Procedure==

# In a metal 1-[[Cookbook:Quart|quart]] mixing bowl, dissolve coffee in water.
# Add the chocolate and set on top of a pan of gently [[Cookbook:Simmer|simmering]] water.
# When the chocolate has softened completely but is not hot, remove from heat and stir until smooth.
# [[Cookbook:Beat|Beat]] in the cold butter a small piece at a time, adding a new piece as soon as the previous one is almost absorbed.
# Beat with a [[Cookbook:Mixer|hand-held electric mixer]] until creamy, about 10 minutes.
# Continue beating for a few minutes to cool. This can also be done in a stand mixer, fitted with the whip attachment.
# Add half of the jalapeños and taste. Add more jalapeño to your taste; remember that the heat will intensify with time. Try for a balance of sweet and heat.
# Scrape into a small, deep container, press a piece of plastic wrap on the surface, and chill overnight, until completely firm.
# Scoop out small balls and roll in the cocoa powder.
# Keep refrigerated until ready to serve.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Roll the balls in finely chopped pistachios, almonds, or macadamia nuts.
